steps.title: Your TV. Your comfort.
steps.explanation: Set up both connections with pictures. This preview does not monitor or change TV audio.

steps.title: Which TV do you use?
steps.explanation: Choose the brand on your TV or remote.
steps.example: Example: if the remote says Samsung, choose Samsung. If you cannot find a name, choose Not sure / no TV.

steps.title: Use a home app?
steps.explanation: Choose the home app you use. Neither is fine.
steps.example: Example: if you say “Alexa” to an Echo speaker, choose Amazon Alexa. If you manage devices in the Google Home app, choose Google Home.

steps.title: 1. Connect to your TV or home device
steps.explanation: Follow the highlighted pictures on your TV or in its official app.
steps.example: Example: finding a Samsung TV in Alexa does not let this preview control it. Audio Bodyguard would still need its own supported connection and your permission.

steps.title: 2. Connect to your phone
steps.explanation: Open your TV's official phone app and follow the pictures.
steps.example: Example: Audio Bodyguard does not control devices in this preview. Pairing and phone permissions are separate checks.

steps.title: Your next step is ready
steps.explanation: Explore the preview. Replay the pictures anytime from Help.
steps.example: Example: to look at the sample graph, open Insights, then Explore an example. Its values are made up; they are not measurements from your phone.

steps.title: Read the coverage state
steps.explanation: Unknown physical state means the app has not independently checked the sound coming from the speakers. This preview does not provide audio protection.
steps.example: Example: a phone can show a TV as connected while the room is using a separate soundbar. The app must check the actual sound output.

steps.title: Check what is supported
steps.explanation: The six setup checks must be established before a control can become eligible. A connected device alone is insufficient.
steps.example: Example: Bluetooth may report headphones connected while the actual playback route is still unknown.

steps.title: Understand missing history
steps.explanation: No observed events means the app has no session evidence to show. An empty list does not mean everything was safe.
steps.example: Example: A gap while the app was away remains a gap in knowledge.

steps.title: Treat OS hints as clues
steps.explanation: Foreground hints describe a system notification. They cannot verify audible output or another app's playback.
steps.example: Example: A route-change notice is a clue to investigate, not an observation of sound.

steps.title: Find the Options menu
steps.explanation: After leaving this guide, choose Sound to see the option descriptions. All controls there are explanations until a supported device is connected and checked.
steps.example: Example: to learn about quieter evening listening, open Sound and read the Night preset description.

steps.title: Volume needs a supported output
steps.explanation: Volume is unavailable in this simulation. A future change needs an authorized device and verified physical result.
steps.example: Example: A requested volume of 40 percent would not prove the speaker reached that level.

steps.title: Choose a compatible preset
steps.explanation: A Dialogue preset is intended for speech. A Night preset is intended for quieter evening listening. They are planned settings and cannot be applied in this preview.
steps.example: Example: you might want speech to be easier to follow without making loud adverts louder. A future preset would still need to be tested on your speakers.

steps.title: Custom EQ is device-specific
steps.explanation: An equalizer changes the balance of low, middle and high sounds. A compatible device would be needed to apply it. This preview cannot change those sounds.
steps.example: Example: reducing bass would make low, rumbling sounds less strong. Reading this description does not change your TV bass.

steps.title: Find the captions option
steps.explanation: Captions depend on an available track or supported caption mode. This option is unavailable until one is connected.
steps.example: Example: A film's authored English caption track could be selectable on a supported player.

steps.title: Check caption evidence
steps.explanation: The Sound page reports what has been observed. This shell has not discovered or selected a caption track.
steps.example: Example: A label describing captions does not mean captions are currently displayed.

steps.title: Save only confirmed settings
steps.explanation: Save, restore and undo require suitable device settings and verification. This shell has no confirmed settings to use.
steps.example: Example: Undo would propose a return to a verified earlier setting; it cannot assume that return succeeded.

steps.title: Look for a verified change
steps.explanation: A requested change and an observed result are different events. Missing history cannot supply an undo result.
steps.example: Example: A successful button tap is not a verified audio change.

steps.title: Open Advanced options
steps.explanation: After leaving this guide, choose Settings. Advanced options explains device checks, background limits and privacy. These descriptions do not change sound.
steps.example: Example: to learn what is stored on your phone, open Settings and read Privacy and storage.

steps.title: Identify the output path
steps.explanation: Device and route stay Unknown until qualified. A device name or connection notification cannot establish the path of sound.
steps.example: Example: A connected speaker may not be the speaker currently used by a player.

steps.title: Require physical observation
steps.explanation: The app needs a check of what actually comes from the speakers, separate from its own command messages. This preview has no such observation.
steps.example: Example: sending “lower the volume” is only a request. A separate check must confirm the intended speaker really became quieter.

steps.title: Understand background limits
steps.explanation: This screen receives foreground hints only. Leaving the app does not establish continuing protection.
steps.example: Example: Events while the screen is hidden remain unknown.

steps.title: Know what this tour stores
steps.explanation: Only appearance and whether you left the beginner guide are saved locally. TV choices and tutorial progress are temporary. No audio or tutorial analytics are uploaded.
steps.example: Example: Closing the tour lets you reopen any topic from its first step.

steps.title: Check transfer eligibility
steps.explanation: Moving a session is unavailable. A transfer requires authorized endpoints and a verified path between them.
steps.example: Example: Two phones signed in to an account are not, by themselves, a qualified transfer path.

steps.title: Keep the handoff state truthful
steps.explanation: The current screen reports that no transfer path is connected. Completing this tutorial does not change that state.
steps.example: Example: You can finish this lesson while session transfer remains unavailable.

steps.title: Output hardware
steps.explanation: Unknown: no supported output device has been identified and qualified for this app.
steps.example: Example: A connected Bluetooth speaker is a candidate, not proof that AQSS can control it.

steps.title: Qualified path
steps.explanation: Unknown: this exact device, driver and output path have not passed the required checks.
steps.example: Example: Passing an emulator test does not qualify a phone speaker.

steps.title: Permission and authority
steps.explanation: Unknown: permission and authority for a supported action have not been established. This checklist requests neither.
steps.example: Example: An OS permission alone cannot authorize a change to another device.

steps.title: Output route
steps.explanation: Unknown: there is no verified path from an authorized action to the intended output.
steps.example: Example: Headphones can be connected without being the active playback route.

steps.title: Runtime eligibility
steps.explanation: Unknown: there is no qualified running protection path. This screen only receives foreground hints.
steps.example: Example: Leaving the app may suspend it; returning does not fill the gap in observation.

steps.title: Independent observation
steps.explanation: Unknown: there is no independent observation tied to an authorized device transaction.
steps.example: Example: A device saying that a command succeeded is not independent evidence of audible output.

chooseTV.title: Another brand

chooseTV.title: Not sure / no TV
chooseTV.detail: You can explore without a TV. Later, look for the brand and model on the TV label or ask someone to help you find it in the About menu.

chooseHome.title: Amazon Alexa
chooseHome.detail: In the Alexa app, check whether your TV maker offers a compatible skill. Follow that maker’s account-linking instructions. Seeing a TV there does not connect it to Audio Bodyguard.

chooseHome.title: Google Home
chooseHome.detail: In Google Home, check whether your exact TV model can be added. Follow its maker’s setup instructions and review any requested permissions. This preview does not access your Google Home.

chooseHome.title: Both apps
chooseHome.detail: Check the TV maker’s instructions for each app separately. Support in Alexa does not prove support in Google Home. This preview does not access either account.

chooseHome.title: Neither / not sure
chooseHome.detail: No smart-home account is needed to explore. Keep using your TV remote. A future direct TV connection would still need a supported model and your permission.
